description: Run-like Dexie tables by name or row lifecycle fields, with their syntactically verified reference to executionRuns. Repay missing and name-only references through the shared ledger; retain real references or explained exclusions in the inventory.

members.note: createPlan/updatePlan persist the plan lifecycle at lib/db/plans.ts:46 and lib/db/plans.ts:138. The liveQuery at lib/execution/agent-state-bridge.ts:416 reads agentPlans, syncPlan calls ensureRun at lib/execution/agent-state-bridge.ts:331, and ensureRun derives execution:plan:<id> and calls createExecutionRun at lib/execution/agent-state-bridge.ts:106; this reviewed asynchronous derived-id bridge justifies real linkage while retaining the extra plan execution table.

beginAgentTaskAttempt at lib/db/agent-tasks.ts:154 creates an attempt under the task board; linkAgentTaskAttemptExecution at lib/db/agent-tasks.ts:207 later stores schedulerExecutionId. The row also has runId, but these standalone writers never call a ledger writer, so its named run reference remains name-only.

createAgentTeamChildRun at lib/db/agent-team-runtime.ts:102 adds a boundary-checked child execution; other accessors mutate its lease/checkpoint/settlement. The child carries its parent runId, and these writer entrypoints do not call the canonical ledger, so that parent identifier provides name-only linkage rather than a proven canonical execution id.

createSquadRunRecords adds the parent row and directly adds its canonical execution row at lib/ai/agent/team/squad/squad-run-records.ts:180 and lib/ai/agent/team/squad/squad-run-records.ts:217; backfillLegacyTeamRun also directly adds the canonical row at lib/agent-team/legacy-run-history.ts:150. Standalone createAgentTeamRun/updateAgentTeamRun writers do not reach that ledger, and these direct writes do not satisfy the import-bound referenceOverride policy. The table has no canonical reference field, so its conservative classification is none despite the linked squad-creation path.

recordBackgroundTaskStart adds a durable dispatch execution at lib/db/background-tasks.ts:56; recordBackgroundTaskSettle and the Dexie journal update its running/settled/lease state. Its parent/run identifiers do not make those standalone writer entrypoints ledger writers, so backgroundTasks retains name-only linkage and a separate execution lifecycle.

projectBestOfNGroup at lib/best-of-n/projection.ts:24 writes the native group snapshot and visible answer summary under groupId, while refresh/rebuild and sync also replace rows. These are per-contest terminal/running projections, but their writers do not create executionRuns or store a canonical run reference; this extra best-of-N lifecycle therefore remains none.

enqueueBotDelivery at lib/db/bot-event-deliveries.ts:185 creates the trigger delivery lifecycle and claimBotDelivery/failBotDelivery mutate its attempts and lease. runBotDelivery can create a ledger row, but enqueue and other exported persistence writers do not reach that call in their own call graph; executionRunId is therefore name-only under the all-writer rule, not blanket real proof.

saveCalibrationRun at lib/db/calibration-runs.ts:55 puts a completed/running calibration report keyed by runId. The accessor has no ledger writer call and the runId field alone does not establish canonical identity, so this separately persisted calibration execution remains name-only.

replaceCollabRuns at lib/db/collab-run-mirror.ts:47 replaces one organization's run mirror transactionally; rows retain individual remote execution states rather than board definitions. The local mirror writer does not create executionRuns or carry a canonical link field, so the extra collaboration execution projection remains none.

enqueueConnectorInboundJob/claimConnectorInboundJob persist an accepted message's execution lifecycle in lib/db/connector-inbound-jobs.ts:461, and bindConnectorInboundJobExecutionRun stores the later canonical id. The enqueue/claim/settle entrypoints do not themselves maintain the canonical ledger, so executionRunId remains name-only evidence despite the runtime binding path.

enqueueOnlineEval at lib/db/eval-online.ts:86 stores a queued judge decision, and claimQueuedOnlineEvals/setOnlineEvalState advance the same row through running and terminal states. No ledger id or writer is present in these accessors, so the per-judge execution lifecycle remains none as well as being durable queued work.

saveRun at lib/db/eval-runs.ts:17 stores one evaluation report when report.runId exists, with case results owned by that report. The accessor only puts evalRuns and never invokes the canonical ledger; its runId primary identity is name-only linkage, leaving a separate evaluation-run record.

DexieEvalOrchestratorRepository.reserveTask takes the queued-to-running reservation at lib/ai/eval/browser-execution.ts:135; recordEvalAttempt/completeEvalTask and finalization update its persisted attempt/state history. These task writers have no executionRuns bridge or canonical link field, so the per-evaluation task lifecycle remains none.

createHarnessRun deduplicates open harness attempts and adds the row at lib/db/harness-evolution.ts:91; saveHarnessRun and claimHarnessRunLease preserve the independent lifecycle/lease. This accessor module writes no executionRuns row and has no canonical reference field, so harness evolution still owns a separate unlinked run table.

enqueueHostDispatch creates an expiring target-delivery lifecycle at lib/db/host-dispatch-queue.ts:76, and failHostDispatch/completeHostDispatch settle it. The optional runId is copied from the caller at lib/db/host-dispatch-queue.ts:102; no ledger writer is called by these accessors, so this delivery-run reference is name-only.

enqueueInboundMaterialization creates queued status and attempts for one accepted draft at lib/db/inbound-materializations.ts:60; markMaterializationRunning/Completed/Failed update the same job. The writer has no canonical run field or ledger call, so materialization has its own none-linked execution lifecycle.

enqueueIntegrationActionJob at lib/db/integrations.ts:556 records an action job and claimIntegrationActionJob at lib/db/integrations.ts:670 gives it a lease/fencing token; updateIntegrationActionJob settles retries or outcomes. The persistence entrypoints do not write the canonical ledger or carry a canonical run identity, leaving an independently tracked action execution with none linkage.

claimIssueRun at lib/db/issue-runs.ts:108 claims an attempt under an issue (the start lock), bindIssueRunDispatch at :144 binds the engine item it dispatched to, and settleIssueRun at :381 records the outcome/deliverable. An issue can have multiple attempts; these accessors do not write executionRuns or store a canonical reference, so issueRuns is execution debt even though the issue board itself is excluded.

createKnowledgeBaseIngestJob at lib/db/knowledge-bases.ts:350 verifies source ownership and creates queued/phase/progress/attempt state; updateKnowledgeBaseIngestJob advances that individual ingest. There is no ledger writer or canonical link in these accessors, so this directly executed ingest remains an unlinked run table even without a later queue drain.

createDexieMediaJobStore at lib/db/media-generation-jobs.ts:42 implements insert/update/status-guarded transition for one provider generation/download job. It stores provider progress and outcome without an executionRuns id or writer call, so asynchronous generation retains a separate none-linked execution record.

enqueueMemoryJob creates a queued lifecycle in lib/db/memory-governance.ts and failMemoryJob at lib/db/memory-governance.ts:659 advances retries/failure under a fenced worker lease. The table does not carry a canonical run reference and these accessors do not write executionRuns; extraction/distill attempts therefore remain independently tracked.

enqueue puts a pending RPC delivery at lib/db/mobile-outbound-queue.ts:303 and claimNext/markSent/recordFailure mutate its attempts and settlement. Its identity is a paired-client command row rather than an executionRuns id, and no ledger call appears in those persistence entrypoints, so the delivery lifecycle is none-linked.

enqueueOutbound and markSending/markFailed persist platform-send attempts in lib/db/outbound-jobs.ts; startOutboundRunner takes the status claim at lib/connectors/outbound-runner.ts:1076. These sends have delivery/notification identities rather than a canonical execution reference and the table writers do not maintain executionRuns, leaving another none-linked lifecycle.

createProjectMiningRun at lib/db/project-mining-runs.ts:46 starts a preconsent backfill run with scan/enqueue/claim counters; claimProjectMiningRun and transitionProjectMiningRun own its lifecycle. The writer has no canonical run reference or ledger call, so the aggregate mining execution remains none even though child memoryJobs are separately queued.

recordProviderDiagnosticJob puts one diagnostics job at lib/provider-diagnostics/store.ts:27; startProviderDiagnosticJob updates running/completed/failed outcomes while workers probe targets at lib/provider-diagnostics/service.ts:373. These persisted executions are not ledger-backed by their writers, so diagnostics remains a separate none-linked run table.

enqueueRetrievalJob transactionally deduplicates active jobs and inserts a lifecycle row at lib/db/retrieval-control.ts:140; finishRetrievalJob and retryStoredRetrievalJob mutate it. No canonical reference or ledger writer exists in these accessors, so it is run-table debt even though claimNextRetrievalJob currently has no wired production consumer for queue membership.

upsertRunRecord puts one assistant-turn projection at lib/db/run-records.ts:83; the row is keyed by [sessionId+runId] and records active/settled turn state. Its runId is a local numeric turn identity and the writer does not call executionRuns, so the similarly named reference is name-only.

Individual scheduled attempts, unlike scheduledTasks definitions, written through the SchedulerDatabase facade (lib/scheduler/scheduler-db.ts), whose private table getters the detector cannot follow. No writer carries a canonical executionRuns link or ledger call, so the attempt history is none-linked.

queueSiteOperation deduplicates provider intent at lib/db/sites.ts:382 and claimSiteOperation/completeSiteOperation/failSiteOperation manage a leased provisioning or deployment execution. The accessors carry provider operation identity rather than a canonical run id and never invoke the ledger, so this operation lifecycle remains none.

createTwinJob at lib/db/twin-jobs.ts:34 inserts one ingest/distill job; claimNextQueuedJob at lib/db/twin-jobs.ts:96 and completeJob/failJob/requeueJob own the lifecycle and retry count. These accessors do not store a canonical run reference or write executionRuns, leaving twin execution state independently persisted.

createWorkflowBatch creates an aggregate execution for the CSV row set at lib/workflow/apps/batch-service.ts:200; runWorkflowBatch at lib/workflow/apps/batch-service.ts:678 owns its lease and aggregate outcome. Child rows have their own execution, but the batch job itself has a running/terminal lifecycle without a canonical ledger reference or writer, so it remains none-linked run debt.

runWorkflow persists the workflow execution and lease in lib/workflow/runtime/orchestrator.ts. The workflow bridge calls createExecutionRun at lib/execution/workflow-bridge.ts:113 for the derived workflow run identity, providing reviewed asynchronous linkage under referenceOverride=real; workflowRuns still duplicates the canonical execution lifecycle even though the static writer-local proof cannot follow that bridge.

acceptWorkSubmission creates the accepted dispatch intent in lib/work-submission/service.ts and can maintain a canonical ledger row, but claimWorkSubmission/renewWorkSubmissionLease in lib/db/work-submissions.ts are independent exported writers. Those entrypoints do not all call a ledger writer, so the stored executionRunId supports name-only rather than universal real linkage for the submission lifecycle.

FusionLedgerStore.createRun at lib/router-fusion/db/ledger-store.ts:607 persists the leased Fusion execution; its transition path enqueues an execution_run_projection outbox effect at lib/router-fusion/db/ledger-store.ts:467. The projection is asynchronous across files and no writer-local canonical ledger call is proven for every entrypoint, so its runId is name-only rather than a real reference override.

excluded.reason: createAgentTask at lib/db/agent-tasks.ts:32 stores a board definition with dependencies/schedule/approval policy; beginAgentTaskAttempt at lib/db/agent-tasks.ts:154 creates a separate attempt. One board row can have many executions, which are inventoried as agentTaskAttempts.

putAgentTeamBoardRows at lib/db/agent-team-board.ts:164 stores the one-way team/task display projection; status and completedAt mirror other entities rather than giving each row an execution identity. agentTeamRuns owns the parent run lifecycle.

writeAgentTeamDefinitions at lib/db/agent-team-definitions.ts:159 persists portable Squad configuration/roster; running that definition creates agentTeamRuns and child runs, so the reusable team is not one execution.

writeAgentTeamDefinitions at lib/db/agent-team-definitions.ts:159 persists portable task definitions with assignments/dependencies; a task can be attempted by multiple agentTeamChildRuns under agentTeamRuns, which are the execution members.

The accountAttemptIndex in lib/plugin/auth/auth-attempts.ts stores OAuth correlation state/PKCE redirect progress; completing an authorization handshake binds credentials rather than representing a requested work run.

beginBotRunStep at lib/db/bot-run-steps.ts:33 returns memoized output for a completed named step under runId; these are step-only records beneath the botEventDeliveries parent member, not another parent execution table.

putBrowserSubmission at lib/db/browser-submissions.ts:108 stores bounded browser side-panel receipts with workId and capture metadata; the durable execution identity is workSubmissions, so side-panel submission state is not counted again.

createGoal at lib/db/goals.ts:42 stores a long-lived session/project commitment; multiple turns can advance it, and the agent-state bridge projects execution runs rather than equating one goal with one execution.

replaceCollabIssues at lib/db/collab-issue-mirror.ts:67 replaces remote issue-board state by organization/revision; an issue can have many issueRuns, so mirrored board status is not an individual execution lifecycle.

replaceCollabPlans at lib/db/collab-plan-mirror.ts:56 refreshes shared plan definitions/steps for an organization; this is a remote collaboration mirror rather than a locally owned plan execution attempt.

recordCleanupFailure at lib/db/connector-cleanup-jobs.ts:107 increments retry/nextAttemptAt for a cache-key delete, and success removes the intent; it has no per-run mutable lifecycle status and is counted as durable queued deletion work instead.

putDerivedProfiles replaces deployment selection/configuration documents with the derived profile set at lib/db/provider-profiles.ts:67; deployment profiles describe model/account routing, not a claimed job or one execution. The unresolved Zod-inferred row is explicitly reviewed rather than silently ignored.

createSquadRunRecords writes the canonical ledger at lib/ai/agent/team/squad/squad-run-records.ts:217; this inventory measures extra run tables relative to that authority, so the canonical executionRuns table is excluded by definition.

putHarnessStep at lib/db/harness-evolution.ts:209 records round/dimension reflection and evidence under runId; parent harnessEvolutionRuns is already a member, so these step-only attempts are excluded.

createIssue at lib/db/issues.ts:134 stores a project board commitment with stage/title/ownership; issueRuns creates separate running/settled attempts, so board state does not make each issue one execution.
createLoop at lib/db/loops.ts:29 stores a persistent loop policy attached to a session/project; repeated iterations can execute under that commitment, so a loop definition is not one work attempt.

requestMcpSync at lib/mcp/sync-coordinator.ts:114 reuses the agentId-keyed desired-configuration row and drainMcpSyncJobs overwrites its running/succeeded state at lib/mcp/sync-coordinator.ts:42; many synchronizations share one row, so it is durable projection work rather than one row per execution.

appendDeliveryAttempt at lib/db/notification-delivery.ts:163 appends outcome/error/receipt evidence for an intentId; attempts are send observations without an independently mutable execution lifecycle, while delivery intents own runnable work.

importPerformanceCapture at lib/perf/capture-portability.ts:354 validates and imports a profiling package; capture recording/import status describes renderer performance artifacts rather than a business job/run execution.

ProviderCatalogAliasRow intersects ModelAlias with revisionId at lib/db/provider-catalog.ts:38; alias rows map model names inside an immutable catalog revision and are neither executable work nor execution records.

ProviderCatalogModelRow intersects ModelDefinition with revisionId at lib/db/provider-catalog.ts:36; model capability/pricing definitions belong to a catalog snapshot, without a queue consumer or one-run lifecycle.

ProviderCatalogOfferingRow intersects ProviderOffering with revisionId at lib/db/provider-catalog.ts:37; offerings are provider/model availability metadata, not tasks awaiting a runner or execution instances.
ProviderCatalogProviderRow intersects ProviderDefinition with revisionId at lib/db/provider-catalog.ts:35; rows define providers in a catalog version and have no claim/drain or execution lifecycle.

ProviderCatalogRevisionRow uses staged/active/previous at lib/db/provider-catalog.ts:27 to select catalog snapshots and stores provider/model/offering counts; that publication state is not a work-attempt status or a durable queue.

recordProviderDiagnosticSample at lib/provider-diagnostics/store.ts:34 persists a target probe measurement beneath providerDiagnosticJobs; the parent diagnostics execution is already a run-table member, so sample/step status is excluded.

putDerivedProfiles bulkPuts provider configuration documents at lib/db/provider-profiles.ts:79 and bumps a CAS profileVersion; these secret-free provider settings are definitions without a drain loop or per-execution lifecycle.

Recurring trigger/config definitions behind the SchedulerDatabase facade (lib/scheduler/scheduler-db.ts); one task can fire repeatedly, and scheduledTaskRuns stores the execution attempts counted by this inventory.

createSiteVersionDraft at lib/db/sites.ts:260 persists an immutable build version and artifact metadata; provisioning/deploy execution belongs to the siteOperations member rather than the reusable artifact version.

SyncFieldClocksRow extends RowClocks with table/rowId and unknown field clocks at lib/account-sync/data/types.ts:32; applyRecord in the sync applier merges conflict clocks, while accountSyncInbox/outbox own runnable synchronization work. Clock metadata is not an execution.

putDerivedProfiles replaces transport configuration documents at lib/db/provider-profiles.ts:80; these profiles describe provider transport settings, not work to claim or an execution attempt, despite the unresolved imported schema type.

wikiBuildJobs is dormant: createWikiBuildJob at lib/db/wiki-build-jobs.ts:81, transitionWikiBuildJob at lib/db/wiki-build-jobs.ts:130, saveWikiBuildCursor at lib/db/wiki-build-jobs.ts:161 and promoteBuild at lib/db/wiki-build-jobs.ts:217 have no production callers or consumers. lib/wiki/orchestrator.ts and rebuild-runner.ts do not read this table or resume its cursor; accessors alone do not establish a running queue or execution owner.

submitHumanInput at lib/db/workflow-human-input.ts:204 resolves a run/step-specific human-input wait; workflowRuns is the parent execution member, and pending/completed here describes a subordinate decision step.

submitHumanInput at lib/db/workflow-human-input.ts:204 records answers against requestId and the owning workflow run; submitted payloads and participant decisions are step evidence beneath workflowRuns, not standalone executions.

FusionLedgerStore records provider-call prepare/dispatch/settle attempts under the fusionRuns parent in lib/router-fusion/db/ledger-store.ts; abandon at lib/router-fusion/db/ledger-store.ts:1455 settles a call reservation, so these step-only attempts are not counted as another parent run table.
